name: Can a feasibility assessment stop me from wasting design money?

mainEntity.name: How can a construction feasibility assessment save money before architectural design starts?
mainEntity.text: How can a construction feasibility assessment save money before architectural design starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: One of the main reasons to order a feasibility assessment early is to avoid paying for a design that never should have been drawn in the first place. If a site cannot support the desired square footage, parking, basement depth, or access plan, it is better to learn that before schematic design is complete. A strong assessment can also reveal where a smaller redesign might preserve the project while reducing cost and risk. In Los Angeles and surrounding cities, this can be especially valuable on tight lots, hillside sites, or properties with aging infrastructure. The assessment should help align the project scope with the site reality and the available budget. Owners should see it as an insurance policy against design churn, permit surprises, and construction change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: A feasibility assessment can prevent wasted design fees by revealing early whether the program is too large, too costly, or too constrained for the site. It helps owners avoid fully designing a project that later fails zoning, grading, utility, access, or budget tests.
